The promotion had a working relationship with Mexico's Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre (CMLL) from 2007 to 2009 and later with Lucha Libre AAA Worldwide (AAA) since 2015, including the Impact vs Lucha Underground show at WrestleCon in April 2018 and the co-promoted Ultra Clash supershow in Monterrey on November 26, 2023 [d454401s16p0].
The promotion worked with Japanese organizations including Inoki Genome Federation (IGF), New Japan Pro-Wrestling (NJPW) (initially 2008–2011 and re-established in February 2021 until December 2024), Wrestle-1 (co-producing the Kaisen: Outbreak supershow in Tokyo on March 2, 2014), and Pro Wrestling Noah [d454401s16p0].
The promotion also had agreements with United States and independent promotions such as the original Global Force Wrestling, OMEGA Championship Wrestling, Evolve Wrestling, and a long list of co-promotional partners for house shows and streaming specials since 2018 including Future Stars of Wrestling, Smash Wrestling, House of Hardcore and others [d454401s16p0].
The promotion entered a partnership with All Elite Wrestling (AEW) in December 2020 that ended quietly in October 2021, and had cross-appearances with WWE acts including Knockouts champions entering the Royal Rumble in 2022 and 2024 and a wider talent exchange beginning in 2024 leading to a announced multi-year partnership with WWE on January 16, 2025 [d454401s16p0].

The promotion later re-established a relationship with NJPW in February 2021 that lasted until December 2024 when NJPW's AXS TV contract expired and was not renewed [d454401s16].

The promotion and AAA co-promoted the Ultra Clash supershow in the Monterrey, Mexico area on November 26, 2023, marking the promotion's first show in Mexico since 2019 [d454401s16].
The promotion established partnerships to co-promote house shows and special events with numerous North American independent promotions since 2018, including Future Stars of Wrestling, Smash Wrestling, Border City Wrestling, WrestleCade and others [d454401s16].
The promotion began a partnership with All Elite Wrestling (AEW) in December 2020 that allowed talent and titles to appear on each other's programming, with that working relationship ending quietly in October 2021 [d454401s16].
The promotion entered a wider talent exchange with WWE in 2024 and on January 16, 2025 WWE announced a multi-year partnership permitting appearances across NXT, the promotion's programming, select WWE Premium Live Events, and promotion pay-per-views [d454401s16].
